text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- A Turkish cougar helicopter crashed during a cross-border operation into northern Iraq, killing eight officers, two non-commissioned officers and a private.
- High-ranking generals will sue Islamist Welfare Party (RP) deputy Sevki Yilmaz for his fiery speeches.
MILLIYET
- General Staff will hold a second briefing for the media on the issue of Islamist extremism.
- Annual inflation, which has reached 80 percent, will soar because of the policies of the Islamist-led government.
HURRIYET
- The executive board of the conservative True Path Party (DYP) objects to forming an election alliance with Welfare, which is currently its partner in the ruling coalition.
- Turkey's role in international money laundering will be debated at an OECD meeting held in Rome.
YENI YUZYIL
- Welfare seeks a way of avoiding closure by the constitutional court. A case opened at the constitutional court recently calls for the party's closure on the grounds that it endangers secularism.
- Businessmen are worried that another election will lead the country to total economic collapse.
RADIKAL
- A Turkish court decision that the pro-Kurdish People's Democratic Party (HADEP) has close relations with rebel Kurdish guerrillas opens the way to closing down the party.
- Turkish exportation rose by 29 percent in May.
DUNYA
- Turkey's second biggest oil tanker burned after an explosion killing four in Istanbul.
- The governor of the Turkish Development Bank promises credit will be made available to develop the impoverished southeast of the country.
ZAMAN
- Some trade unionists object to a declaration prepaped by five leading unions in support of the secularist state structure because it does not deal with workers' problems.
CUMHURIYET
- Private school fees have risen by more than 400 percent in the past 10 years.
